study: Stereo RGB height relative to the first paused camera query
panel: All 527 original stereo camera queries in the six TRAIN teacher episodes of P1_REGISTRATION.json (sha256 1d496553b347a43c6f5c45c99d736896060ca9d71bf6cd5a72fef3e767b1b900). Include both colors and every query. Primary analysis uses the instructed color. No new captures.
sensor: Use original uint8 body and wrist RGB with same-timestamp camera_calibration (the replaced body camera paired with the original wrist). Run the same estimator for both colors. Never pass actor state, teacher stage, segmented geometry, depth, model predictions or target instruction into stereo estimation.
method: For each color require dominant channel minus either other channel >=25 and dominant >=1.3 times either other channel. Choose largest 8-connected component with at least 16 pixels per view; deterministic scan-order ties. Use visible bounding-box center with pixel centers at i+0.5. Triangulate the midpoint between closest points on directed calibrated optical rays. Abstain if a component is missing, intersection angle is under 2 degrees or over 178 degrees, either forward depth is nonpositive, or closest separation exceeds 15 mm. Record the reason.
predicate: Require a valid height at the first scheduled stereo query. For each later query use only its estimate and the fixed initial estimate. Positive when delta_z >= 20 mm. Missing either gives an explicit abstention. Compare to same sampled physical height using each episode's first query as baseline, not to native grasp or continuous task success.
readout: Keep complete episode/query denominators. Report 3D and signed/absolute relative height errors, true/false positive/negative and abstention split by observed physical height, per-episode first sampled crossings and maximal height; detail both target and distractor. The query clock is 0.5 s. No data-dependent parameter changes or native admission based on these results.
